en.q: Which of the following can thermodynamics NOT tell us about a reaction?
o: The rate at which it proceeds
The extent to which it proceeds
en.sol: Thermodynamics looks only at initial and final states. Rate and mechanism belong to chemical kinetics.

en.q: The laws of thermodynamics are applicable to:
o: Macroscopic systems with a very large number of molecules
en.sol: NCERT stresses that thermodynamics deals with macroscopic (bulk) systems, not microscopic ones.

en.q: For practical purposes in thermodynamics, the surroundings are:
o: The entire universe except the system
That portion of the rest of the universe which can interact with the system
en.sol: Formally the surroundings are everything except the system, but in practice only the region that can interact with the system matters.

en.q: Which statement about the boundary of a thermodynamic system is correct?
o: It must always be a physical wall
It can be real or imaginary
It never allows energy to pass
It is part of the surroundings only
en.sol: The boundary can be a real wall (beaker) or an imaginary surface defined by coordinates.

en.q: A cup of hot tea kept on a table (without lid) is an example of:
en.sol: Vapour (matter) escapes and heat (energy) is lost, so both matter and energy are exchanged: an open system.

en.q: Reactants sealed in a stoppered steel flask constitute a/an:
en.sol: Matter cannot leave a sealed flask, but steel conducts heat, so energy can be exchanged: a closed system.

en.q: For an isolated system, which is always true?
en.sol: No heat or work crosses the boundary, so ΔU = q + w = 0. Entropy can still increase in a spontaneous change.

hi.note: Hindi pending: waiting for the NCERT Hindi term glossary (neet-sources).

en.q: Coffee kept in a perfectly sealed and insulated thermos flask is an example of:
en.sol: Neither matter nor energy can cross the boundary.

en.q: A thermodynamic state function is a quantity:
o: Whose value is independent of path
Whose value depends on temperature only
en.sol: By definition, a state function depends only on the state of the system, not on how that state was reached.

en.q: Which of the following is NOT a state function?
en.sol: Work depends on the path. U, H and S are state functions.

en.q: Which combination is a state function?
en.sol: q + w = ΔU, which is a state function even though q and w individually are not.

en.q: For a fixed amount of an ideal gas, how many of p, V and T must be specified to fix its state?

en.q: The internal energy of a closed system can change by:
en.sol: In general U changes by heat, work or matter transfer. A closed system cannot exchange matter, so only heat and work remain.

en.q: For a process to occur under adiabatic conditions, the correct condition is:
en.sol: Adiabatic means no heat exchange with the surroundings, so q = 0.

en.q: Joule's experiments with paddle-churning and electrical heating of water in an insulated vessel showed that:
o: Mechanical work produces more heat than electrical work

en.sol: Equal amounts of adiabatic work by different routes gave the same temperature rise, so U is a state function.
